nodes.definition: A named research investigation, identified by `session_id`. Contains a motivation brief, search tags, queries, papers, catalog entries, and report. Persisted as a set of JSON artifacts on disk.
A term extracted from the research brief, carrying a context-specific `definition`, `synonyms` (feeds search tag generation), and `role` (construct, variable, method, outcome, or context).

A classification of terms derived from KeyConcepts. Three categories: primary_terms (strong relevance signal), supporting_terms (secondary signal), exclusion_terms (out-of-scope indicator). Also includes domain_tags, methodology_tags, and key_authors.

A search string variant generated from SearchTags, carrying a formatted string, target endpoint, filters, execution order, and variant type classification (broad, narrow, methodological, author-focused, venue-focused, or temporal).
A campaign within a research session, grouping queries and their collected scholarly documents. Manages the lifecycle of query execution, result collection, and document acquisition.

Structured findings extracted from an approved scholarly work. Contains bibliographic data, relevance score, extraction confidence, research alignment (hypothesis support/contradiction + evidence type), findings (main claim, key results, conclusions, limitations, future work), methodology (study design, sample size, dataset, methods/tools), evidence (key metrics with values, direct quotes), and related DOIs.

Classification of a scholarly work's contribution type: empirical quantitative, empirical qualitative, systematic review, meta-analysis, theoretical, case study, or mixed. Used for filtering, tagging, and thematic grouping.
The final synthesised output (defined by the output schema). Contains summary, hypothesis verdicts, and supporting evidence from catalog entries.

The report's assessment of the stated hypothesis: `supported`, `contradicted`, `mixed`, `insufficient_evidence`, or null (no hypothesis). Includes confidence score and supporting/contradicting DOI lists.
Quality indicators on a structured finding when extraction is imperfect. Examples: short source, OCR noise, missing methods, paywall partial.
The human actor operating the Research Distillery system. Includes researchers, scholars, and graduate students conducting academic research.
The automated Research Distillery application that processes research queries, manages pipelines, and produces reports.
The system component responsible for creating, tracking, and persisting research sessions throughout their lifecycle.
The system component that executes queries against scholarly search APIs and retrieves paper metadata.
The system component that scores retrieved papers across multiple relevance dimensions and produces ranked lists with accept/reject decisions.
The system component responsible for fetching full-text PDFs from open-access sources and Sci-Hub for accepted papers.
The system component that parses downloaded PDFs and extracts structured content for catalog entry generation.
The system component that assembles the research catalog into a structured report with hypothesis verdicts and sufficiency assessments.
The system component that stores and retrieves all research session artifacts (briefs, queries, papers, catalogs, reports) on disk.
The system component that generates co-citation and citation link data from the paper set for visualisation in the catalog view.
The system component that generates citation files in standard formats (BibTeX, APA, MLA, Chicago) for selected papers.
The shared system component that intercepts failures across pipeline stages and presents actionable remediation options to the user.
Structured research brief derived from the user's free-text research question, containing hypotheses, scope constraints, and key concepts.
A structured piece of information extracted from a paper, containing a statement, supporting evidence, and optional confidence score.
An extracted assertion from a paper with supporting and contradicting evidence.
A thematic grouping of catalog entries with a consensus summary showing supporting and contradicting source counts.
Citation network data containing co-citation links between authors and citation links between papers.
A co-citation link between two authors, recording how many times they are cited together.
Metadata for an exported research session archive, including format, path, and included papers.
A single clarification Q&A turn between user and system during research brief refinement.
A user edit or redaction to a catalog entry, recording the original and replaced values with timestamp.
Possible outcomes for a hypothesis verdict: supported, contradicted, inconclusive, or not applicable.
Assessment of whether collected sources constitute an adequate review.

A scholarly document such as a paper, conference proceeding, preprint, or technical report. Identified by a unique identifier. May be retrieved via scholarly search APIs or imported from citation managers.
A logged system event recording a failure with context (session, source, failure code) and suggested recovery actions.
Lifecycle status of a source within a research session, from ranked through extracted or rejected.
An observational study where two groups are compared — one with the outcome of interest (cases) and one without (controls).
A descriptive study tracking patients with a known exposure or treatment, without a control group.
A high-level study that identifies, appraises, and synthesizes all relevant studies on a research question.
A study that observes a population at a single point in time to assess prevalence.
A study design that combines quantitative and qualitative research methods.
Research conducted in a controlled environment outside a living organism (e.g., cell culture).
Research conducted within a living organism (e.g., animal studies).
A PDF source that contains many mathematical formulas, which may have extraction errors.
A PDF that is a scanned image rather than text, potentially with poor OCR quality.
A source written in a language other than English, which may have translation gaps.
A verdict outcome indicating the hypothesis is not applicable to the collected evidence.
A sufficiency verdict indicating more sources are needed to reach adequate coverage.
A citation link between two authors, recording how many times they are cited together in the literature.
A citation link between two scholarly sources, recording that one source cites another.
A lightweight metadata snapshot of a research session, including title, status, and references to its queries, papers, catalog entries, and report.
A single chat communication exchanged between the user and the system within a research session, carrying role (user/system), content, and timestamp.
A curated collection of scholarly sources organized by the user, containing multiple research sessions and their associated papers, findings, and reports.

Machine-readable error codes used to classify system failures, including network errors, parsing errors, download failures, rate limits, authentication failures, storage errors, validation errors, and unknown errors.
Error severity levels used to prioritise error handling and user notification.
Query execution lifecycle status, tracking a query from creation through execution to completion or failure.
Origin of a query: whether it was manually entered by the user, automatically generated from search tags, or derived from a similar source.
Search campaign lifecycle status, tracking whether a search is currently running, has completed, or was cancelled.
Suggested recovery actions for a logged error event, providing actionable remediation options to the user.
Optional filter criteria used when querying research sessions, including status, text search, and library scope.
A testable statement about the expected relationship between variables, derived from the research question and refined through the clarification process.
The free-text question provided by the user that defines the scope and objective of the research session.
A numerical score computed by the ranking engine that indicates how well a paper matches the research question, used for accept/reject decisions.
A formatted list of citations for selected papers, exported in standard academic formats such as BibTeX, APA, MLA, or Chicago.
The complete persisted state of a research session including all artifacts, ensuring zero data loss after transient failures.
A citation management tool (e.g., Zotero, Mendeley) from which users can import paper lists into a research session.
A temporary failure in the pipeline (e.g., network timeout, API rate limit) that may resolve on retry without user intervention.
The degree of agreement among catalog entries on a finding, measured by supporting versus contradicting source counts within a thematic cluster.
Bibliographic information about a scholarly source including title, authors, abstract, publication year, journal, and DOI, retrieved from search APIs.
The user's explicit decision to include or exclude a borderline-scored paper from further processing.
A packaged export of a complete research session including report, catalog, and metadata, suitable for sharing or backup.
The process of verifying the identity of a user or system component before granting access to resources.
The process of categorizing papers or findings into predefined categories or taxonomies.
The unsupervised grouping of papers or findings based on similarity, used for thematic analysis.
A structured data store (relational or document-based) used for persistent storage of application data.
The process of extracting structured information (findings, claims, metadata) from unstructured PDF documents.
The process of selecting a subset of items based on specified criteria.
A significant word or phrase extracted from text, used for indexing and search.
The process of transferring data between storage systems, formats, or databases.
Portable Document Format, a file format used for distributing documents, commonly used for scholarly papers.
The process of analyzing a string of symbols (text or structured data) to determine its grammatical structure.
The process of ordering papers or results by relevance score or other criteria.
The act of attempting an operation again after a failure, often with exponential backoff.
The process of assigning a numerical value to indicate quality, relevance, or confidence.
A blueprint or definition of the structure of data, including field names, types, and constraints.
A specific release or iteration of a software component, document, or data model.
